grammar_contract.input: An ordinary parse-that child-parser state at any source-native UTF-16 offset from 0 through source.length, with an arbitrary predecessor value and either empty or nonempty diagnostic state.
grammar_contract.operation: Inspect at most the next three source positions through direct parse-that terminals/combinators and return true exactly for sign+digit, sign+dot+digit, dot+digit, or digit; otherwise false.
grammar_contract.composition: The harness constructs string(prefix).map(variedPredecessor).next(candidate).skip(string(continuation)); the outer parser, not the harness, invokes the candidate child parser.
grammar_contract.consumption: Always succeed, replace the predecessor with one boolean, consume zero code units, and leave the following grammar at the original candidate offset.
grammar_contract.diagnostics: Preserve furthest, expected, suggestions, and secondarySpans byte-for-byte on true and false under both empty and seeded state.
grammar_contract.diagnostic_sandbox: Candidate recognition must use direct parse-that terminals/combinators. A candidate-local Parser wrapper may snapshot and restore only parse-that diagnostic bookkeeping around speculative recognition. It may not inspect or slice state.src, classify characters, advance a cursor, or feed a token/CST layer.
grammar_contract.preprocessing: Only ASCII +, -, ., and 0–9 can form a positive prefix. CSS preprocessing cannot create a positive case from CR, CRLF, FF, NUL, lone surrogates, astral scalars, or other non-ASCII units, so raw and preprocessed truth are identical for this operation.
grammar_contract.work_bound: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space, no token/CST/substrings/arrays proportional to source length, and no imperative scanner.
